role.zh: 赖阿特阿岛航海家、祭司、画家

summary.en: A high priest of ʻOro from Raʻiatea who joined Cook's Endeavour at Tahiti in 1769. He drew a chart of some 74 islands from memory, interpreted for Cook with Māori in New Zealand and painted the earliest known Indigenous pictures of the encounter, before dying of disease at Batavia.
summary.zh: 来自赖阿特阿岛的奥罗神大祭司，1769年在塔希提登上库克的“奋进号”。他凭记忆绘出约74座岛屿的海图，在新西兰为库克与毛利人传译，并留下已知最早由太平洋原住民绘制的接触场景画作，最终在巴达维亚病逝。

label.en: Born at Raʻiatea, trained at Taputapuātea
label.zh: 生于赖阿特阿岛，在塔普塔普阿特阿受训

label.en: Flees Bora Bora invasion to Tahiti; adviser to Purea
label.zh: 因波拉波拉入侵逃往塔希提，成为普雷亚的顾问

label.en: Joins the Endeavour at Matavai Bay
label.zh: 在马塔瓦伊湾登上“奋进号”
在图朗加努伊阿基瓦与毛利人交谈传译

sources.title: Te Ara / Dictionary of New Zealand Biography: Tupaia
J. Salmond, Aphrodite's Island: The European Discovery of Tahiti (University of California Press, 2009)
British Library: Drawings by Tupaia

story.en:
Tupaia was a navigator-priest of the war god ʻOro, schooled at Taputapuātea on Raʻiatea. When warriors from Bora Bora overran his island he fled to Tahiti, where he became adviser to the chiefess Purea and met Samuel Wallis in 1767 and James Cook in 1769.

Joseph Banks persuaded Cook to take him aboard. Tupaia guided the Endeavour through the Society Islands and, with the help of the officers, set down a chart of islands he knew, drawn in the Polynesian way from his own position rather than from north. In New Zealand his speech was close enough to Māori that he could talk with local chiefs, and Māori long remembered the ship as 'Tupaia's ship'. Watercolours once credited to an anonymous artist, including a Māori trading a crayfish with Banks, are now known to be his.

Scurvy and fever weakened him on the Australian coast, and he died at Batavia in December 1770, shortly after his young assistant Taiata.
story.zh:
图帕伊亚是战神奥罗的航海祭司，曾在赖阿特阿岛的塔普塔普阿特阿接受训练。波拉波拉的武士攻占他的家乡后，他逃往塔希提，成为女酋长普雷亚的顾问，并在1767年和1769年先后结识塞缪尔·沃利斯与詹姆斯·库克。

约瑟夫·班克斯说服库克让他上船。图帕伊亚引导“奋进号”穿行社会群岛，并在军官协助下画出他熟知的岛屿海图，这张图按波利尼西亚方式以自身位置而非正北为基准。在新西兰，他的语言与毛利语相近，能与当地酋长交谈，毛利人长期把这艘船称为“图帕伊亚的船”。一组曾被认为出自无名画家之手的水彩画，包括一名毛利人用龙虾与班克斯交换物品的场景，如今已确认是他的作品。

在澳大利亚海岸，坏血病和热病使他日渐虚弱，1770年12月，他在年轻助手泰阿塔死后不久卒于巴达维亚。

role.zh: 荷兰航海家（荷兰东印度公司）

summary.en: Commander of the VOC's 1642–43 expedition that reached Tasmania, New Zealand, Tonga and Fiji, and of a 1644 survey of northern Australia. He showed that New Holland was not joined to a southern continent within reach, but found nothing the Company could trade.
summary.zh: 荷兰东印度公司1642–1643年远征的指挥官，到达塔斯马尼亚、新西兰、汤加和斐济，1644年又勘察了澳大利亚北部海岸。他证明新荷兰并不与可及范围内的南方大陆相连，却没有找到公司可以贸易的东西。

label.zh: 生于格罗宁根省卢特赫斯特
在巴达维亚为荷兰东印度公司效力

label.en: Clash with Ngāti Tūmatakōkiri at Mohua (Golden Bay)
label.zh: 在莫胡阿（金湾）与恩加蒂图马塔科基里人冲突
测绘澳大利亚北部海岸

sources.title: Te Ara / Dictionary of New Zealand Biography: Tasman, Abel Janszoon
Britannica: Abel Tasman

role.zh: 西班牙航海家

summary.en: Led two Spanish voyages from Peru in search of a rich southern land: in 1568 he reached and named the Solomon Islands, and in 1595 he sighted the Marquesas before dying at a failed colony on Nendö in the Santa Cruz Islands. His widow Isabel Barreto took the survivors to Manila.
summary.zh: 两度率西班牙船队从秘鲁出发寻找富庶的南方大陆：1568年到达并命名所罗门群岛；1595年发现马克萨斯群岛，随后死于圣克鲁斯群岛恩德尼岛上失败的殖民地。其遗孀伊莎贝尔·巴雷托率幸存者驶往马尼拉。

label.zh: 抵达所罗门群岛圣伊莎贝尔岛
发现并命名马克萨斯群岛
卒于恩德尼岛格拉西奥萨湾

sources.title: Britannica: Álvaro de Mendaña de Neira
O. H. K. Spate, The Spanish Lake (ANU Press, 1979)

name.zh: 路易-安托万·德·布干维尔

role.zh: 法国航海家、军人

summary.en: Led the first French circumnavigation (1766–69). His nine days at Tahiti in 1768 and his book of 1771 made the island Europe's image of a 'New Cythera'. He also named Bougainville Island; his ship carried Jeanne Barret, the first woman known to circle the globe.
summary.zh: 率领法国首次环球航行（1766–1769）。他1768年在塔希提停留九天，1771年出版的游记使该岛成为欧洲人心目中的“新基西拉”。他还命名了布干维尔岛；其船上的让娜·巴雷是已知第一位完成环球航行的女性。

label.zh: 在福克兰群岛建立路易港
停泊于塔希提岛希蒂阿阿
驶经并命名布干维尔岛

sources.title: Britannica: Louis-Antoine, comte de Bougainville
L.-A. de Bougainville, Voyage autour du monde (1771)

role.zh: 英国海军军官、探险家

summary.en: A Yorkshire farm labourer's son who rose through the merchant marine and Royal Navy to command three Pacific voyages (1768–79). He charted New Zealand and eastern Australia, crossed the Antarctic Circle and reached Hawaiʻi, where he was killed at Kealakekua Bay in 1779.
summary.zh: 约克郡农工之子，经商船队和皇家海军逐级晋升，指挥了三次太平洋航行（1768–1779）。他测绘了新西兰和澳大利亚东海岸，越过南极圈并抵达夏威夷，1779年在凯阿拉凯夸湾被杀。

label.en: Surveys the St Lawrence before Quebec
label.zh: 在魁北克战前测绘圣劳伦斯河

label.en: Observes the transit of Venus at Tahiti
label.zh: 在塔希提观测金星凌日

label.en: First recorded crossing of the Antarctic Circle
label.zh: 有记录以来首次穿越南极圈

sources.title: Britannica: James Cook
J. C. Beaglehole, The Life of Captain James Cook (Hakluyt Society, 1974)

story.en:
James Cook was born in 1728 at Marton in Yorkshire, the son of a Scottish farm labourer. Apprenticed to a Whitby shipowner, he learned his seamanship in colliers on the North Sea and volunteered for the Royal Navy in 1755. His charts of the St Lawrence before the capture of Quebec in 1759, and of Newfoundland in the 1760s, made his name as a surveyor.

Given command of the Endeavour in 1768, he made three Pacific voyages in eleven years. He mapped New Zealand and the east coast of Australia, sailed farther south than anyone before him without finding a habitable southern continent, and kept scurvy largely at bay. His ships carried Tupaia, Mai and other islanders, and his journals are among the richest European records of Pacific societies at the moment of contact.

The voyages also opened the way to colonisation: Botany Bay was chosen for the convict settlement on the strength of his first voyage. Cook was killed at Kealakekua Bay in February 1779 when an attempt to take the chief Kalaniʻōpuʻu hostage went wrong. In Britain he became a national hero; for many Aboriginal Australians, Māori and Hawaiians his arrival marks the beginning of invasion and loss, and his statues have become sites of protest.
story.zh:
詹姆斯·库克1728年生于约克郡马顿，父亲是苏格兰籍农场雇工。他在惠特比一位船主手下当学徒，在北海的运煤船上学会航海，1755年志愿加入皇家海军。他在1759年攻取魁北克之前测绘圣劳伦斯河，又在18世纪60年代测绘纽芬兰，由此以测量专家闻名。

1768年他受命指挥“奋进号”，此后十一年间三次远航太平洋。他测绘了新西兰和澳大利亚东海岸，向南航行得比前人都远，却没有找到可居住的南方大陆，并在很大程度上遏制了坏血病。他的船载过图帕伊亚、迈等岛民，他的航海日志是欧洲人记录接触之初太平洋社会最丰富的资料之一。

这些航行也为殖民打开了大门：正是凭借第一次航行的报告，英国选定植物学湾建立流放地。1779年2月，库克在凯阿拉凯夸湾试图把酋长卡拉尼奥普乌扣为人质，事态失控，他被杀身亡。在英国他成了民族英雄；而在许多澳大利亚原住民、毛利人和夏威夷人看来，他的到来标志着入侵与丧失的开始，他的雕像也成了抗议的场所。

role.en: First Governor of New South Wales
role.zh: 新南威尔士首任总督

summary.en: Royal Navy captain who commanded the First Fleet and founded the penal colony at Sydney Cove in 1788. He kept the starving settlement alive, sought conciliation with the Eora while kidnapping men to learn their language, and returned to England in 1792.
summary.zh: 皇家海军上校，指挥第一舰队并于1788年在悉尼湾建立流放殖民地。他使饥荒中的定居点得以维持，一面寻求与伊奥拉人和解，一面掳人学习其语言，1792年返回英国。

label.en: Sails with the First Fleet from Portsmouth
label.zh: 率第一舰队从朴次茅斯启航

label.en: Founds the settlement at Sydney Cove

sources.title: Australian Dictionary of Biography: Phillip, Arthur
Britannica: Arthur Phillip

role.en: Wangal man, intermediary between the Eora and the colony
role.zh: 旺加尔人，伊奥拉族与殖民地之间的中间人

summary.en: A Wangal man captured on Phillip's orders in 1789, Bennelong escaped, then chose to deal with the newcomers, helping to end a cycle of reprisals. A hut was built for him on what is now Bennelong Point; he sailed to England in 1792 and returned in 1795.
summary.zh: 旺加尔人，1789年被菲利普下令掳走，后逃脱，又主动与外来者打交道，帮助终止了冤冤相报的循环。殖民者在今天的本尼朗角为他建造小屋；1792年他远赴英国，1795年回国。

label.en: Born in Wangal Country on the Parramatta River
label.zh: 生于帕拉马塔河畔旺加尔人之地
在图博古勒（本尼朗角）建屋
与耶梅拉瓦尼同在伦敦

sources.title: Australian Dictionary of Biography: Bennelong
K. V. Smith, Bennelong: The Coming in of the Eora (Kangaroo Press, 2001)
Dictionary of Sydney: Bennelong

story.en:
In November 1789, after smallpox had ravaged the harbour clans, Phillip had two men seized at Manly Cove so the colony could learn their language. One was Bennelong, a Wangal man of perhaps 25 with a sharp wit and a scarred body. He was kept in irons, dined at the governor's table and escaped in May 1790.

In September that year Phillip went to meet him at a whale feast at Manly; in the confusion another man speared the governor through the shoulder. Phillip forbade reprisals, and soon afterwards Bennelong came in to Sydney on his own terms. He asked for a brick hut on the point at Tubowgule, which still bears his name beneath the Opera House.

In 1792 he and the younger Yemmerrawanne sailed to England with Phillip; Yemmerrawanne died there. Bennelong returned in 1795, moving between colonial and Eora worlds, and died at Kissing Point in 1813. Settler obituaries mocked him; Aboriginal descendants remember him as a diplomat.
story.zh:
1789年11月，天花刚刚重创港湾各氏族，菲利普下令在曼利湾掳走两名男子，以便殖民地学习他们的语言。其中之一就是本尼朗，一位约25岁、机智而遍体伤疤的旺加尔人。他戴着镣铐，在总督餐桌上用餐，1790年5月逃走。

同年9月，菲利普到曼利的一次鲸肉宴上与他相见；混乱中另一名男子用长矛刺穿了总督的肩膀。菲利普禁止报复，不久本尼朗按自己的条件来到悉尼。他要求在图博古勒岬角建一座砖屋，那里至今以他的名字命名，就在悉尼歌剧院之下。

1792年，他与年轻的耶梅拉瓦尼随菲利普前往英国，耶梅拉瓦尼客死异乡。本尼朗于1795年回国，往来于殖民者与伊奥拉人两个世界之间，1813年卒于基辛角。殖民者的讣告嘲讽他，原住民后裔则把他铭记为一位外交家。

role.zh: 比吉加尔人抵抗领袖

summary.en: A Bidjigal man of the Botany Bay–Georges River district who led armed resistance to the colony for twelve years, raiding farms around Parramatta and the Hawkesbury. Shot in 1797 and captured, he escaped in irons; he was killed in 1802 and his head was sent to Joseph Banks in England.
summary.zh: 植物学湾—乔治河一带的比吉加尔人，领导对殖民地的武装抵抗长达十二年，袭击帕拉马塔和霍克斯伯里一带的农场。1797年他中弹被俘，却戴着镣铐逃脱；1802年被杀，头颅被送往英国的约瑟夫·班克斯处。

label.en: Born in Bidjigal Country near Botany Bay
label.zh: 生于植物学湾附近比吉加尔人之地
用长矛刺死菲利普的猎场看守麦金太尔

label.en: Wounded at the battle of Parramatta
label.zh: 在帕拉马塔之战中负伤

label.en: Shot dead in the Parramatta district
label.zh: 在帕拉马塔一带被枪杀

sources.title: Australian Dictionary of Biography: Pemulwuy
National Museum of Australia: Defining Moments – Pemulwuy

note: Birth year is approximate (c. 1750); the exact place of his death is not recorded.

role.en: Founder of the Kingdom of Hawaiʻi
role.zh: 夏威夷王国开创者

summary.en: A Hawaiʻi Island chief who, using European guns and advisers alongside traditional warfare, conquered Maui, Molokaʻi and Oʻahu by 1795 and secured Kauaʻi's submission in 1810. His law of the splintered paddle protected non-combatants.
summary.zh: 夏威夷岛酋长，在传统战法之外借助欧洲枪炮和顾问，到1795年征服毛伊、莫洛凯和瓦胡，1810年使考艾岛归附。他颁布的“断桨法”保护非战斗人员。

label.zh: 生于科哈拉的科科伊基
在凯阿拉凯夸会见库克船队
在莫库奥海击败基瓦拉奥
在努乌阿努征服瓦胡岛
在火奴鲁鲁接受考艾岛归附

sources.title: Britannica: Kamehameha I
S. M. Kamakau, Ruling Chiefs of Hawaii (rev. ed. 1992)

note: Birth year is uncertain (estimates range from c. 1736 to 1761); 1758 follows the tradition of a birth under Halley's Comet.

story.en:
Hawaiian tradition says Kamehameha was born under a bright comet, often identified with Halley's Comet of 1758, and that his life was in danger from birth because a prophecy named him a killer of chiefs. As a young warrior under his uncle Kalaniʻōpuʻu he boarded Cook's ships in 1779.

When Kalaniʻōpuʻu died, Kamehameha defeated his heir Kīwalaʻō at Mokuʻōhai in 1782. Following a prophecy, he built the great temple of Puʻukoholā, where his last rival on the island, Keōua, was killed at the dedication in 1791. With two British sailors he had detained, the Englishman John Young and the Welshman Isaac Davis, as gunners, he invaded Maui and, in 1795, Oʻahu, where at Nuʻuanu many defenders were driven over the cliffs of the Pali.

Two invasions of Kauaʻi failed, but in 1810 its king Kaumualiʻi accepted his rule. Kamehameha remembered being struck with a paddle by a fisherman during a raid; his Kānāwai Māmalahoe, the law of the splintered paddle, let the elderly, women and children travel unharmed.
story.zh:
夏威夷传统说，卡美哈梅哈出生时天上有一颗明亮的彗星，常被认为是1758年的哈雷彗星；又因预言称他将杀死诸酋长，他自出生起就面临生命危险。年轻时他在叔父卡拉尼奥普乌麾下作战，1779年曾登上库克的船。

卡拉尼奥普乌死后，卡美哈梅哈于1782年在莫库奥海击败其继承人基瓦拉奥。他依照预言修建了宏伟的普乌科霍拉神庙，1791年落成之际，他在岛上的最后一个对手凯奥瓦被杀。他以两名被扣留的英国水手——英格兰人约翰·扬和威尔士人艾萨克·戴维斯——为炮手，进攻毛伊岛，并于1795年进攻瓦胡岛，在努乌阿努许多守军被逼坠下帕利悬崖。

两次进攻考艾岛均告失败，但1810年考艾国王考穆阿利伊接受了他的统治。卡美哈梅哈记得自己在一次袭掠中被渔夫用船桨击中；他颁布的“断桨法”保障老人、妇女和儿童通行无虞。

role.en: Queen and kuhina nui of Hawaiʻi
role.zh: 夏威夷王后、库希纳努伊（共治者）

summary.en: Kamehameha I's favourite wife, who after his death in 1819 claimed the new office of kuhina nui, co-ruler with the king. She helped abolish the kapu system, converted to Christianity in 1825 and made Protestant morality the law of the kingdom.
summary.zh: 卡美哈梅哈一世最宠爱的妻子。1819年国王去世后，她出任新设的“库希纳努伊”，与国王共治。她推动废除禁忌制度，1825年皈依基督教，并把新教道德定为王国法律。

label.en: Proclaims herself kuhina nui; ʻAi Noa at Kailua
label.zh: 在凯卢阿自立为库希纳努伊，推动“自由共食”
在火奴鲁鲁卡瓦伊阿哈奥受洗

sources.title: Britannica: Kaahumanu
J. Silverman, Kaahumanu: Molder of Change (Friends of the Judiciary History Center, 1987)

story.en:
Kaʻahumanu was born around 1768 near Hāna on Maui, the daughter of the chief Keʻeaumoku, one of Kamehameha's closest allies. She married Kamehameha around 1785 and became his favourite and most politically important wife; Europeans who met her remarked on her stature, intelligence and strong will.

When Kamehameha died in May 1819, she told his heir Liholiho that the late king had wished her to share in ruling, and so created the office of kuhina nui. Within months she and Keōpūolani, the king's highest-ranking wife and Liholiho's mother, persuaded the new king to eat with women, breaking the ʻai kapu that had ordered Hawaiian society for centuries. When chiefs loyal to the old gods rose under Kekuaokalani, her forces defeated them at Kuamoʻo.

She was wary of the American missionaries who arrived in 1820, but after a serious illness she embraced their teaching and was baptised in 1825. As regent for the boy king Kamehameha III, she toured the islands promoting schools and churches and in 1827 proclaimed laws against murder, theft and other offences drawn from Christian morality. She died in Mānoa valley in 1832, having steered Hawaiʻi through one of the deepest changes in its history.
story.zh:
卡阿胡马努约1768年生于毛伊岛哈纳附近，父亲凯埃奥莫库是卡美哈梅哈最亲密的盟友之一。约1785年她嫁给卡美哈梅哈，成为他最宠爱、政治上也最重要的妻子；见过她的欧洲人都提到她身材高大、聪慧而意志坚强。

1819年5月卡美哈梅哈去世后，她对继承人利霍利霍说先王希望由她共同执政，由此设立了“库希纳努伊”一职。数月之内，她与先王地位最高的妻子、利霍利霍之母凯奥普奥拉尼说服新王与女性同食，打破了维系夏威夷社会数百年的饮食禁忌。忠于旧神的酋长们在凯库阿奥卡拉尼率领下起兵，被她的军队在库阿莫奥击败。

她起初对1820年到来的美国传教士心存戒备，但在一场重病之后接受了他们的教义，并于1825年受洗。作为少年国王卡美哈梅哈三世的摄政，她巡行各岛推广学校与教会，1827年颁布以基督教道德为依据、禁止谋杀和盗窃等罪行的法令。1832年她在马诺阿山谷去世，此前她带领夏威夷度过了其历史上最深刻的变革之一。

role.zh: 恩加普希部落战争领袖

summary.en: A Ngāpuhi rangatira who protected the first missionaries at Rangihoua, visited England in 1820, and used the muskets he acquired to launch devastating campaigns across the North Island, opening the Musket Wars.
summary.zh: 恩加普希部落的酋长，曾在朗伊霍瓦保护最早的传教士，1820年访问英国，并用获得的火枪对北岛各地发动毁灭性征战，揭开“火枪战争”的序幕。

label.en: Hosts Samuel Marsden's mission at Rangihoua
label.zh: 在朗伊霍瓦接待塞缪尔·马斯登的传教团

label.en: At Cambridge helping compile a Māori grammar
label.zh: 在剑桥协助编写毛利语语法
攻破塔玛基的毛伊纳伊纳堡寨
攻陷怀帕地区的马塔基塔基

sources.title: Te Ara / Dictionary of New Zealand Biography: Hongi Hika
R. D. Crosby, The Musket Wars (Reed, 1999)

role.zh: 恩加蒂托阿部落战争领袖

summary.en: Led Ngāti Toa from Kāwhia to Kapiti Island in the 1820s and from there dominated Cook Strait, raiding the South Island. He composed the haka 'Ka Mate'. After the Wairau clash of 1843 he was seized by Governor Grey in 1846 and held without trial.
summary.zh: 19世纪20年代率恩加蒂托阿部落从卡菲亚迁往卡皮蒂岛，进而称雄库克海峡并袭掠南岛。他创作了哈卡战舞《卡马特》。1843年怀劳冲突后，1846年他被格雷总督逮捕并未经审判关押。

label.en: Leads Ngāti Toa south from Kāwhia
label.zh: 率恩加蒂托阿部落从卡菲亚南迁

sources.title: Te Ara / Dictionary of New Zealand Biography: Te Rauparaha
NZHistory: Te Rauparaha

story.en:
Te Rauparaha was born at Kāwhia, probably in the 1760s, to a Ngāti Toa father and a Ngāti Raukawa mother. According to tradition, around 1820 he composed the haka 'Ka Mate' while hiding from pursuers in a kūmara pit near Lake Rotoaira, sheltered by the chief Te Wharerangi.

Hard pressed by Waikato and Ngāti Maniapoto, he led Ngāti Toa on a long migration south in 1821–22 and seized Kapiti Island, which commanded Cook Strait. From there, armed with muskets traded from passing ships, he raided deep into the South Island. In 1830 the captain of the brig Elizabeth helped him capture the Ngāi Tahu chief Tamaiharanui at Akaroa, and in 1831–32 his warriors took the great pā at Kaiapoi.

When settlers came he sold land, and disputed it, with the New Zealand Company. In June 1843 a confrontation over surveying of the Wairau valley, which he denied selling, left 22 settlers and at least four Māori dead. Governor Grey had him seized in 1846 and held without trial for about eighteen months. He returned to Ōtaki and died there in 1849, remembered both as a formidable strategist and as the author of New Zealand's best-known haka.
story.zh:
特劳帕拉哈大约生于18世纪60年代，出生地在卡菲亚，父亲属恩加蒂托阿部落，母亲属恩加蒂劳卡瓦部落。据传说，约1820年他为躲避追兵藏身于罗托艾拉湖附近的甘薯窖中，得到酋长特法雷朗伊的庇护，并在此创作了哈卡战舞《卡马特》。

在怀卡托和恩加蒂马尼亚波托部落的压迫下，他于1821至1822年率恩加蒂托阿部落长途南迁，夺取扼守库克海峡的卡皮蒂岛。此后他凭借从过往船只换来的火枪，深入南岛袭掠。1830年，“伊丽莎白号”双桅船船长协助他在阿卡罗阿擒获恩加伊塔胡部落酋长塔迈哈拉努伊；1831至1832年，他的战士攻陷了凯阿波伊大型堡寨。

移民到来后，他向新西兰公司出售土地，也与之争执地权。1843年6月，双方因测量怀劳河谷（他否认曾出售此地）发生冲突，22名移民和至少4名毛利人死亡。1846年格雷总督下令将他逮捕，未经审判关押约一年半。他回到奥塔基，1849年在那里去世。人们既记得他是一位令人生畏的战略家，也记得他是新西兰最著名哈卡的作者。

role.zh: 布鲁尼岛努恩农人女性

summary.en: A Nuenonne woman who survived the violence of the Black War, guided George Augustus Robinson's 'Friendly Mission', endured exile at Wybalenna and Oyster Cove, and was falsely called 'the last Tasmanian'. Her skeleton was displayed in a museum until 1947 and cremated in 1976.
summary.zh: 努恩农族女性，她在“黑色战争”的暴力中幸存，曾为乔治·奥古斯塔斯·鲁宾逊的“友好使团”带路，经历怀巴伦纳和牡蛎湾的流放，却被错误地称为“最后的塔斯马尼亚人”。她的遗骨在博物馆展出至1947年，1976年火化。

label.zh: 加入鲁宾逊的“友好使团”
被流放到弗林德斯岛怀巴伦纳

label.en: Taken to Port Phillip with Robinson
label.zh: 随鲁宾逊前往菲利普港

sources.title: Australian Dictionary of Biography: Truganini
L. Ryan, Tasmanian Aborigines: A History since 1803 (Allen & Unwin, 2012)

story.en:
Truganini grew up on Bruny Island in the years when sealers and whalers abducted Aboriginal women; before she was twenty, her mother had been killed, her sister taken and her betrothed murdered. In 1830 she joined George Augustus Robinson, a builder turned 'conciliator', as he walked the island persuading the surviving clans to surrender.

The promise was safety and a return to Country. Instead the people were shipped to Wybalenna on Flinders Island, where most died of disease and despair. Truganini went with Robinson to Port Phillip in 1839; there she and others joined a band that killed two whalers, and two of the men were hanged in Melbourne in 1842, the first public execution there.

She ended her days at Oyster Cove and in Hobart, dying in 1876 afraid of what scientists would do with her body. Her fear was justified: her skeleton was exhibited at the Tasmanian Museum. It was finally cremated in 1976 and her ashes scattered on the D'Entrecasteaux Channel. Palawa people today reject the myth that she was the 'last' of them.
story.zh:
特鲁加尼尼在布鲁尼岛长大，那时海豹猎人和捕鲸者常掳走原住民妇女；不到二十岁，她的母亲被杀，姐妹被掳，未婚夫遇害。1830年，她加入由建筑工人转为“调解人”的乔治·奥古斯塔斯·鲁宾逊，随他徒步全岛，劝说幸存的氏族投降。

许诺是安全和重返故土，结果族人却被运往弗林德斯岛的怀巴伦纳，多数人死于疾病与绝望。1839年特鲁加尼尼随鲁宾逊去了菲利普港；在那里她与其他人加入一伙人，杀死了两名捕鲸者，其中两名男子于1842年在墨尔本被绞死，这是当地首次公开处决。

她在牡蛎湾和霍巴特度过余生，1876年去世时仍害怕科学家会处置她的遗体。她的担忧成了现实：她的骨骸在塔斯马尼亚博物馆展出。直到1976年遗骨才被火化，骨灰撒入当特尔卡斯托海峡。今天的帕拉瓦人拒绝接受她是族人中“最后一位”的说法。

role.zh: 塔希提女王

summary.en: Queen of Tahiti for fifty years from 1827. Her expulsion of French Catholic missionaries gave France a pretext for the protectorate of 1842; she fled to Raʻiatea during the Franco-Tahitian War and returned in 1847 to reign under French oversight.
summary.zh: 自1827年起统治塔希提长达五十年。她驱逐法国天主教传教士之举，成为法国1842年建立保护国的借口；法塔战争期间她逃往赖阿特阿岛，1847年返回，在法国监管下继续在位。

sources.title: Britannica: Pomare IV
C. Newbury, Tahiti Nui (University of Hawaii Press, 1980)

role.zh: 怀卡托酋长，首任毛利王

summary.en: A renowned Waikato war leader of the Musket Wars who refused to sign the Treaty of Waitangi but protected early Auckland. In old age he accepted the kingship, installed at Ngāruawāhia in 1858, and died two years later.
summary.zh: 怀卡托部落在火枪战争中赫赫有名的战争领袖，他拒绝签署《怀唐伊条约》，却保护了初建的奥克兰。晚年他接受王位，1858年在恩加鲁阿瓦西亚即位，两年后去世。

攻占塔拉纳基的普克朗伊奥拉

role.en: Taranaki prophet and leader of non-violent resistance
role.zh: 塔拉纳基先知、非暴力抵抗领袖

summary.en: A Te Āti Awa prophet who, with Tohu Kākahi, founded the community of Parihaka in the 1860s and resisted confiscation of Taranaki land by ploughing, fencing and passive defiance. Arrested when troops invaded Parihaka in 1881, he was held without trial until 1883.
summary.zh: 特阿蒂阿瓦部落的先知，19世纪60年代与托胡·卡卡希一起建立帕里哈卡社区，以犁地、筑篱和消极抗命等方式抵制塔拉纳基土地被没收。1881年军队入侵帕里哈卡时被捕，未经审判关押至1883年。

label.zh: 与托胡·卡卡希建立帕里哈卡

label.zh: 在帕里哈卡遭入侵时被捕

role.en: Vunivalu of Bau, King of Fiji
role.zh: 包岛武尼瓦卢、斐济国王

summary.en: Warlord of the small island of Bau who styled himself Tui Viti, converted to Christianity in 1854, reigned as king of a settler-run Fijian government from 1871, and in 1874 ceded Fiji to Queen Victoria.
summary.zh: 小岛包岛的军事领袖，自称“图伊维提”（斐济之王），1854年皈依基督教，1871年起出任由移民主导的斐济政府的国王，1874年把斐济割让给维多利亚女王。

name.zh: 乔治·图普一世（陶法阿豪）

role.zh: 汤加国王

summary.en: A Haʻapai chief who converted to Methodism in 1831, defeated his rivals and by 1845 ruled all Tonga as Tuʻi Kanokupolu. He freed commoners from chiefly bondage in 1862, granted the 1875 constitution and guarded Tonga's independence until his death at about 96.
summary.zh: 哈派群岛酋长，1831年皈依卫理宗，击败对手，到1845年以图伊卡诺库波卢身份统治全汤加。1862年他解除平民对酋长的依附，1875年颁布宪法，并一直捍卫汤加的独立，约96岁时去世。

label.zh: 在利富卡受洗，取名乔治

label.en: Becomes Tuʻi Kanokupolu, king of all Tonga
label.zh: 成为图伊卡诺库波卢，统治全汤加

S. Lātūkefu, Church and State in Tonga (ANU Press, 1974)

role.en: Last monarch of the Kingdom of Hawaiʻi; composer
role.zh: 夏威夷王国末代君主、作曲家

summary.en: Queen from 1891, she tried to restore royal and Native Hawaiian voting power curtailed by the 1887 Bayonet Constitution and was overthrown in 1893. Imprisoned in ʻIolani Palace after the failed 1895 rising, she later lobbied in Washington against annexation. She wrote 'Aloha ʻOe'.
summary.zh: 1891年即位，力图恢复被1887年“刺刀宪法”削减的王权和夏威夷原住民投票权，1893年被推翻。1895年起义失败后被囚禁于伊奥拉尼宫，后在华盛顿游说反对吞并。她创作了歌曲《珍重再见》（Aloha ʻOe）。

label.en: At Queen Victoria's Golden Jubilee, London
label.zh: 在伦敦出席维多利亚女王登基五十周年庆典

label.en: Imprisoned in the palace; forced to abdicate

label.zh: 在华盛顿游说反对吞并
卒于火奴鲁鲁华盛顿宫

sources.title: Britannica: Liliuokalani
Liliʻuokalani, Hawaii's Story by Hawaii's Queen (1898)

story.en:
Lydia Kamakaʻeha was born in Honolulu in 1838 into a high chiefly family and, following Hawaiian custom, was raised by hānai (adoptive) parents. Educated at the Royal School with other young aliʻi, she married the American-born John Owen Dominis and in 1877 was named heir to her brother, King Kalākaua, taking the name Liliʻuokalani.

A gifted musician, she composed more than 150 songs, including 'Aloha ʻOe'. In 1887 she represented the kingdom at Queen Victoria's Golden Jubilee in London, and came home to find that an armed group of white businessmen had forced Kalākaua to accept the 'Bayonet Constitution', which curbed royal power and, through property qualifications, took the vote from many Native Hawaiians while excluding Asian residents altogether.

She became queen in January 1891. Her move to proclaim a new constitution in January 1893 prompted the Committee of Safety, backed by US marines, to depose her. After the failed royalist rising of 1895 she was arrested, signed an abdication in the hope of saving her jailed supporters, and was confined in an upstairs room of ʻIolani Palace for about eight months. She spent her remaining years campaigning against annexation, published Hawaii's Story by Hawaii's Queen in 1898, and died at Washington Place in 1917.
story.zh:
莉迪亚·卡马卡埃哈1838年生于火奴鲁鲁一个高级酋长家庭，按夏威夷习俗由“哈奈”（收养）父母抚养长大。她与其他年轻的阿利伊一同在皇家学校接受教育，嫁给美国出生的约翰·欧文·多米尼斯，1877年被立为兄长卡拉卡瓦国王的继承人，改名利留卡拉尼。

她极具音乐天赋，创作了150多首歌曲，其中包括《珍重再见》（Aloha ʻOe）。1887年她代表王国赴伦敦出席维多利亚女王登基五十周年庆典，回国后发现一伙武装的白人商人已逼迫卡拉卡瓦接受“刺刀宪法”。这部宪法削弱王权，并以财产资格剥夺了许多夏威夷原住民的投票权，亚裔居民则被完全排除在外。

1891年1月她即位为女王。1893年1月她准备颁布新宪法，此举促使得到美国海军陆战队支持的“安全委员会”将她废黜。1895年保王派起义失败后，她被逮捕，为解救狱中的支持者签署了退位书，并被囚禁在伊奥拉尼宫楼上的一个房间里约八个月。此后她余生都在反对吞并，1898年出版《夏威夷女王讲述夏威夷的故事》，1917年在华盛顿宫去世。

role.zh: 妇女参政运动家

summary.en: Liverpool-born leader of the Women's Christian Temperance Union franchise campaign in New Zealand, who organised the great petitions of 1891–93 that won women the vote in 1893. She became the first president of the National Council of Women in 1896 and appears on the NZ$10 note.
summary.zh: 生于利物浦，领导新西兰基督教妇女禁酒联合会的选举权运动，组织了1891至1893年的大规模请愿，使妇女于1893年获得投票权。1896年出任全国妇女理事会首任主席，形象印在新西兰10元纸币上。

label.zh: 向议会递交选举权请愿书

role.zh: 尤里卡栅栏起义领袖、政治家

summary.en: An Irish engineer turned gold digger who led the Ballarat miners' oath under the Southern Cross flag in 1854 and lost an arm when troops stormed the stockade. Hidden by friends, he was never tried, and he later served as Speaker of the Victorian Legislative Assembly.
summary.zh: 爱尔兰工程师出身的淘金者，1854年在南十字旗下带领巴拉瑞特矿工宣誓，军队攻破栅栏时失去一条手臂。他被朋友藏匿，从未受审，后来出任维多利亚立法议会议长。

role.zh: 西阿兰达族画家

summary.en: A Western Arrernte man from Hermannsburg mission whose watercolours of the MacDonnell Ranges made him the most famous Aboriginal artist of his time. Granted citizenship in 1957, a status most Aboriginal people were denied, he was convicted in 1958 of supplying alcohol to a kinsman, served two months' detention in 1959 and died that August.
summary.zh: 来自赫曼斯堡传教站的西阿兰达族人，他描绘麦克唐奈山脉的水彩画使他成为当时最著名的原住民艺术家。1957年他获得公民权，而多数原住民当时并无此资格；1958年他因给亲属提供酒类被定罪，1959年服刑两个月，同年8月去世。

role.zh: 汤加女王、诗人

summary.en: Queen for 47 years, she healed rifts among Tongan chiefly lines, promoted education and health, and composed many songs and poems. Riding in an open carriage through London's rain at Elizabeth II's coronation in 1953, she won British affection.
summary.zh: 在位47年，她弥合了汤加各酋长世系之间的裂痕，推动教育和卫生事业，并创作了大量歌谣与诗歌。1953年伊丽莎白二世加冕礼上，她冒雨乘敞篷马车穿过伦敦街头，赢得英国民众的喜爱。

summary.en: A Hokianga leader of Te Rarawa who developed Māori land schemes, became founding president of the Māori Women's Welfare League in 1951 and, at 79, led the 1975 land march from Te Hāpua to Parliament under the slogan 'not one more acre'.

summary.en: A Gurindji stockman who in August 1966 led some 200 workers and their families off Vestey's Wave Hill station, turning a strike over pay and conditions into a claim for land. In 1975 Prime Minister Whitlam poured soil into his hand as part of a lease handback.
summary.zh: 古林吉族牧工，1966年8月带领约200名工人及家属离开维斯蒂公司的韦夫山牧场，把一场争取工资与待遇的罢工变成对土地的诉求。1975年，惠特拉姆总理在归还租约的仪式上把一把泥土倒入他的手中。

role.zh: 梅里亚姆人土地权利活动家

summary.en: A Meriam man from Mer in the Torres Strait who worked as a labourer and university gardener in Townsville. Learning that his family's land legally belonged to the Crown, he led the ten-year case that overturned terra nullius in 1992, months after his death.
summary.zh: 来自托雷斯海峡梅尔岛的梅里亚姆人，曾在汤斯维尔做工人和大学园丁。得知自家土地在法律上属于王室后，他领导了长达十年的诉讼，1992年推翻“无主地”原则，而那时他已去世数月。

label.zh: 参与创办黑人社区学校

label.en: Lodges the land claim; hearings in Brisbane
label.zh: 提起土地诉讼，在布里斯班开庭

sources.title: Australian Dictionary of Biography: Mabo, Edward Koiki
National Museum of Australia: Defining Moments – Mabo decision

role.zh: 萨塔瓦尔岛航海大师

summary.en: A pwo navigator from Satawal in the Caroline Islands who guided the Hawaiian voyaging canoe Hōkūleʻa to Tahiti in 1976 without instruments, proving the feasibility of Polynesian wayfinding, and then taught Nainoa Thompson and others, reviving traditional navigation across the Pacific.
summary.zh: 加罗林群岛萨塔瓦尔岛的“普沃”级航海师，1976年不借助仪器引导夏威夷航海独木舟“霍库莱阿号”抵达塔希提，证明了波利尼西亚传统导航的可行性，随后传授给奈诺阿·汤普森等人，复兴了太平洋传统航海术。

label.en: Sets out from Maui aboard Hōkūleʻa
label.zh: 乘“霍库莱阿号”从毛伊岛出发
在夏威夷培训奈诺阿·汤普森

label.en: Initiates new pwo navigators on Satawal
label.zh: 在萨塔瓦尔岛为新一代航海师举行“普沃”仪式

sources.title: Polynesian Voyaging Society: Mau Piailug
B. Finney, Hokuleʻa: The Way to Tahiti (Dodd, Mead, 1979)

role.en: First Prime Minister of Papua New Guinea
role.zh: 巴布亚新几内亚首任总理

summary.en: A teacher and broadcaster from East Sepik who co-founded the Pangu Party in 1967, led PNG to self-government in 1973 and independence in 1975, and served as prime minister three times. He is remembered as the 'father of the nation'.
summary.zh: 来自东塞皮克省的教师和广播员，1967年参与创建潘古党，领导巴新于1973年自治、1975年独立，三度出任总理，被尊为“国父”。

label.en: Grows up at Karau, East Sepik
label.zh: 在东塞皮克省卡劳成长

sources.title: Britannica: Sir Michael Somare
M. Somare, Sana: An Autobiography (Niugini Press, 1975)

role.zh: 努纳卡尔族诗人、活动家

summary.en: Born Kath Walker on Minjerribah (North Stradbroke Island), she published We Are Going (1964), the first book of poetry by an Aboriginal woman, campaigned for the 1967 referendum and founded an education centre at Moongalba. In 1987 she returned her MBE in protest at the coming bicentenary.
summary.zh: 本名凯丝·沃克，生于明杰里巴（北斯特拉德布罗克岛），1964年出版的《我们将离去》是首部由原住民女性创作的诗集。她为1967年公投奔走，并在蒙加尔巴创办教育中心。1987年她退还大英帝国勋章，以抗议即将举行的殖民二百周年庆典。

label.en: Serves in the Australian Women's Army Service, Brisbane
label.zh: 在布里斯班加入澳大利亚妇女陆军服务队
创办蒙加尔巴教育中心

sources.title: Australian Dictionary of Biography: Noonuccal, Oodgeroo
National Museum of Australia: Collaborating for Indigenous Rights – Oodgeroo Noonuccal

name.zh: 图普阿·塔马塞塞·莱阿洛菲三世

role.en: Samoan paramount chief and Mau leader
role.zh: 萨摩亚最高酋长、马乌运动领袖

summary.en: A holder of one of Samoa's paramount titles who led the non-violent Mau movement against New Zealand rule. Exiled to New Zealand in 1928, he returned in 1929 and was shot by New Zealand police during a Mau procession in Apia on 28 December 1929, Black Saturday.
summary.zh: 萨摩亚最高称号之一的持有者，领导反对新西兰统治的非暴力马乌运动。1928年被流放新西兰，1929年回国，同年12月28日“黑色星期六”在阿皮亚的马乌游行中被新西兰警察枪杀。

label.en: Exiled and jailed in New Zealand
label.zh: 被流放并关押于新西兰

label.en: Shot during the Mau procession in Apia
label.zh: 在阿皮亚马乌游行中中弹

sources.title: NZHistory: Black Saturday
M. Field, Mau: Samoa's Struggle for Freedom (Polynesian Press, 1991)
